sessionTitle: Agent supervision is the new senior engineering skill

announcements.name: Cognition shipped an agent command centre
announcements.shortDescription: Announced "yesterday," it features local-to-cloud handoff and follows the same multi-agent "conductor" form factor as Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, and GitHub Copilot.
announcements.longDescription: Swix notes that Cognition, a company he advises, shipped an agent command centre the day before, converging on the same multi-agent 'conductor' form factor as Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, and GitHub Copilot. It includes interesting features such as local-to-cloud handoff. He frames this as the industry shifting focus away from managing individual agents toward more organized multi-agent orchestration.

announcements.name: OpenAI is merging Codex into ChatGPT
announcements.shortDescription: Presented as evidence that coding-world workflows are bleeding into general knowledge work.
announcements.longDescription: Swix cites as a 'fun fact' that the OpenAI team announced the day before that they are merging Codex into ChatGPT. He presents this as evidence that what happened to coding last year is now bleeding into general knowledge work, with developers getting to preview that future first.

announcements.name: GitHub commit growth cited at 14,000x year-on-year
announcements.shortDescription: Attributed to a podcast conversation with the GitHub CEO; Claude Code attribution on GitHub is described as rising from ~4-5% in February toward a projected 50% by year end.
announcements.longDescription: Referencing a podcast he released with the GitHub CEO the day before, Swix cites a figure of roughly 14,000x year-on-year commit growth on GitHub. He also notes that Claude Code [inferred] attribution on GitHub rose to 4-5% as of February, is probably around 10% currently, and is on trend to reach 50% by end of year, with similar dynamics expected from Codex, Copilot, and other coding agents.

announcements.name: Cerebras collaboration on high-speed inference
announcements.shortDescription: Cognition is working with Cerebras on models delivering thousands of tokens per second.
announcements.longDescription: Swix explains that for massively parallel agents you want them to finish as quickly as possible, and that Cognition has been working closely with Cerebras [inferred] on models (referenced as 3, 1.5, and 3C2 coming up) targeting thousands of tokens per second inference. He contrasts this with typical inference speeds of roughly 50 to 100 tokens per second, and references Talus/Talos demos reaching 17,000 tokens per second, predicting near-instant commodity-token inference is mathematically coming.
